Extract Sequences in Wide Format

Source: R/extract_sequences.R
extract_sequences.Rd

Returns the sequences behind any Nestimate input as a wide data frame, one row per sequence and one column per position. Accepts the output of prepare(), a long event log, a wide data frame or character matrix, a netobject, a grouped netobject_group, or a tna model. Model objects return their stored, decoded states.

Usage

extract_sequences(
  x,
  cols = NULL,
  actor = NULL,
  action = NULL,
  time = NULL,
  meta = FALSE,
  ...
)

Arguments

x

Sequence data: a nestimate_data object from prepare(); a long event log (supply action); a wide data.frame or character matrix; a netobject, netobject_group, cograph_network or tna built from sequence data.

cols

Character vector of state columns for wide data frames. When NULL, numeric columns of a mixed data frame are treated as covariates and the remaining columns as states. Ignored for model objects.

actor, action, time

Column names of a long event log, passed to prepare(). Supplying action marks x as long.

meta

Logical. When TRUE, the covariate columns that belong to each sequence (actor, session, group, metadata) are placed before the state columns. Default FALSE.

...

Further arguments passed to prepare() for long input (e.g. time_threshold, order).

Value

A data.frame with one row per sequence. State columns are character, with NA after a sequence ends; their names are the position names of the input (T1, T2, ... for prepared or long data). With meta = TRUE the covariate columns come first. A grouped network adds its grouping column. Input that has no sequence data raises nestimate_bad_input.

See also

prepare, sequence_patterns

Examples

extract_sequences(trajectories)
#>              1          2          3          4          5          6
#> 1       Active Disengaged Disengaged Disengaged     Active     Active
#> 2      Average    Average    Average    Average    Average    Average

                  action = "Action", time = "Time", meta = TRUE)
